name: Poolside
summary: Poolside builds AI models specialized for writing software and is developing a 2-gigawatt AI data-center campus in Texas.
overview: Poolside develops large language models focused on software development, along with the compute infrastructure to train them.
bull_case: Nvidia backing, a large licensing deal and its own compute give Poolside resources few model startups have.
bear_case: It competes with OpenAI, Anthropic and coding tools like Cursor, and its revenue has not been disclosed.
latest_round: August 2026: reported $1B Nvidia investment at $12B pre-money
directory_notes: Terms of the Nvidia licensing deal.

intelligence.description: Poolside develops large language models focused on software development, along with the compute infrastructure to train them.
company: Poolside was founded in 2023 by Jason Warner, a former GitHub CTO, and Eiso Kant. It builds AI models for coding and software development, released open-weight models including Laguna, and is developing Project Horizon, a 2-gigawatt AI campus in Pecos County, Texas.

Poolside raised a $500 million Series B at a $3 billion valuation in October 2024. Nvidia committed up to $1 billion in October 2025 at a $12 billion valuation, and in August 2026 an investor letter reported by Newcomer described a $6 billion non-exclusive licensing deal with Nvidia plus a $1 billion investment at a $12 billion pre-money valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Poolside is a bet that specialized coding models can compete with general AI labs, and its Nvidia licensing deal is an unusual way for a model company to monetize.

takeaways: The latest figures come from a reported investor letter, not a company announcement.
The Nvidia licensing deal could matter more than the equity raise.
Coding is one of the most competitive areas in AI.
Owning data-center capacity adds capital intensity.
